title: Plan a defensible study
summary: Specify the question, task, scoring, recruitment, analysis and stopping rule before fielding.
steps: Cite prior research with its population, period, method and limits. Separate findings from hypotheses and business priorities; name the decision and its owner.

Define one primary outcome, the unit counted, numerator, denominator, scoring rule, treatment of missing outcomes and smallest difference worth acting on. Distinguish observed task success, self-report and tracking status.

For the current A/B/n activity, one session receives one design. Keep tasks and measurement comparable across designs. A paired study needs a separately suitable design, pairing and order controls; it is not a switch in this A/B activity.

Write a neutral participant task that does not reveal the intended answer. Write the accepted answer or success rubric separately for the scorer, including how partial or ambiguous answers are handled.

Define eligibility, recruitment, access needs, consent, device support and approved data handling before recruitment. Pilot with assistive technology when relevant; record remaining accessibility limits.

Justify the target using precision, power or a formative learning plan. Keep recruited, eligible, assigned, scored and follow-up-completed targets distinct. The comparison display minimum of 10 assigned per design is not a recommended sample size.

The standard A/B primary rate uses everyone assigned; dropout and unmeasured sessions remain in that denominator as not successful, with measurement status reported separately. Recruit extra for losses before assignment; later dropout is not removed from the assigned target. Do not forecast follow-up completion without a stated completion assumption.

Predefine primary contrasts, analysis, exclusions and a stopping rule. Record repeat-session risks: sessions are not verified unique people. Any recruitment controls belong in approved systems, not identifiers sent to an agent.

Pilot the exact versions, collection route, assignment, success signal and follow-up end to end. Recheck the plan after import into the installed Studio version. A generated draft or survey is not permission to field a study.
questions: Can another researcher score the primary outcome without guessing?
Are recruitment, assignment and follow-up targets using the correct units?
What must be checked or approved before real participants can enter?
example: Participant task: You checked your refund status and see that processing is underway. What, if anything, would you do next? Keep the intended interpretation in a separate scorer rubric; do not put it in the participant prompt.
